workDescription:
I am a professional percussionist with more than 15 years of experience. I was born into a family of musicians, so from an early age I began playing the Armenian dhol, a traditional double-headed drum deeply rooted in my cultural heritage. Over the years, I developed my skills across a wide range of professional percussion instruments and techniques, absorbing elements from different cultures and musical traditions and combining them into my own unique playing style.

My main instruments include darbuka, bongos, congas, djembe, cajón, udu, timbales and other percussion, as well as drum kit, although hand percussion is my main specialization. By combining techniques from different instruments, I can adapt my playing to different musical styles and performance formats.

I work across a wide range of styles, including Arabic, Latin, pop, lounge, electronic, house, jazz and live music. One of my strongest skills is improvisation: I quickly pick up rhythmic patterns and respond to the music in real time, adjusting my rhythm, dynamics and sound to make percussion a natural part of the musical arrangement. This works especially well when performing with DJs, adding a human and dynamic element to the set and making each performance unique. My goal is to complement the music rather than simply play over it, while knowing when to step forward and create a strong, energetic solo when the moment calls for it. The approach always depends on the audience, event and stage.

I also enjoy creating stylized performances that combine electronic music with traditional and ethnic influences. Drawing on my experience with different percussion styles and musical traditions, I like creating live remixes and reinterpretations of familiar songs, giving well-known music a fresh and unexpected sound through live percussion.

I can also combine my DJ skills with live percussion and perform as a two-in-one artist, combining both roles within one performance. This format can be built around prepared tracks and rhythmic patterns to achieve a high level of musical and technical quality while incorporating live percussion. When required, I can also prepare and memorize specific performance numbers for an event. I learn new material quickly, which makes preparing special performances and new material straightforward for me.

Alongside my performance experience, I am also the creator of a drum and brass show, which has given me additional experience in performance organization, production and working with different audiences and event formats.

My work explores the relationship between art, emotion, identity, and contemporary living. I work primarily with painting and mixed media, using expressive color, fluid forms, and layered details to create visually rich and emotionally engaging works inspired by personal experiences, cultural references, and the visual language of contemporary life.

My artistic practice extends beyond the traditional canvas. I am passionate about bringing art into everyday spaces through functional and immersive forms, which has led me to explore artist-designed furniture and interior objects. Through this direction, I combine artistic expression, craftsmanship, and refined design to create pieces that carry a strong visual and personal identity.

This vision is embodied in Reem Wassy Casa, a dedicated line under my artistic identity exploring the intersection of contemporary art and functional design. Each piece is conceived not simply as furniture or an interior object, but as an artwork designed to live within a space.

Across painting, mixed media, furniture, and functional art, my practice continues to explore how art can move beyond the canvas and become part of the way we experience and inhabit our everyday environments.

In the Saudi art and AV scene, my role is often to bridge the creative and technical sides of a project. I help clients move from an initial idea or brief into a workable audiovisual experience, whether that means developing the concept, designing the media system, producing sound and visuals, building interactive components, or preparing the work for exhibition, performance, or public presentation.

I also work on proposals, technical documentation, creative direction, and production planning for cultural and institutional projects.

The materials and tools I work with include sound systems, synthesizers, controllers, cameras, sensors, depth cameras, LED screens, projection, CRT displays, Ableton Live, TouchDesigner, real-time visual systems, and custom media workflows. The work can range from small studio sessions and training formats to larger audiovisual installations and commissioned cultural projects.

My background in music, sound, visual programming, and new media art allows Desert.Dream to offer both creative authorship and practical production support. The focus is always to create work that is technically reliable, visually and sonically strong, and appropriate for the context, whether it is an exhibition, workshop, public program, cultural commission, or artist-led project.

The work of artist Salem Awari centers on exploring social and human relationships through a diverse range of approaches and media as a means of communication and understanding the complexities that connect human beings to one another and to the world around them. Through his works, Awari seeks to present a vision that goes beyond the visible to cross toward the invisible, expressing the emotions, experiences, and interactions that form the essence of human relationships.

Awari draws inspiration from everyday life, stories, personal experiences, and social interactions that take place around him, beginning with spontaneous moments, passing incidents, and the small details that may seem ordinary, considering them an endless source of inspiration. He transforms them into artworks that reflect the complexity of social life and human entanglements.

Through his works, he aims to deconstruct social symbols and reshape them in ways that reflect shared experiences, emotions, and social memory that connect us as human beings, presenting questions about the nature of human relationships and how we interact with social values and concepts. Awari uses different media and artistic approaches as tools to explore and analyze these relationships, drawing on mixed-media techniques to add new dimensions to the ideas presented, reflecting the dynamism and complexities of social life. Color and line become visual elements that tell stories of strength and weakness, communication and silence, isolation and connection.

Through his works, Awari presents an ongoing dialogue with the world and with others. The concept of recycling plays a central role in his artworks, not only as a material process but also as a philosophy that reflects the relationship between humans and the environment and their ability to adapt and rebuild. The history and past stories carried by these materials reinforce the concept of communicating with the past and its influence on the present.

workDescription:
I am a Saudi contemporary artist working across painting and material-based practices. My work explores memory, trace, and what remains beneath visible surfaces, with a particular interest in how materials retain evidence of pressure, transformation, and time.

I work primarily with acrylic, gypsum, and gesso, using repeated processes of layering, covering, scraping, fracturing, sanding, and exposing. These processes create tactile surfaces where traces of previous layers remain partially visible, allowing the material itself to become part of the narrative.

My practice is informed by my relationship to place, collective memory, and the material and architectural environment of Saudi Arabia. I am particularly interested in working with materials connected to local landscapes and making traditions, and in translating these references through a contemporary material language rather than through literal representation.

While my practice is rooted in painting, I am currently expanding these material investigations into reliefs, objects, and site-specific spatial installations that respond to architecture, public space, and their surrounding context.
